title: Briefing: India, Albania, Canada, Italy and France
script: This is the Unowned briefing for Saturday, October thirty-first. It's narrated by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our checked timelines.
Every item carries our grade. Confirmed means independent outlets agree. Reported means only one source has it so far. Disputed means the accounts conflict. And alleged is one side's claim.

India. Cockroach Janta Party president Abhijeet Dipke posted an Instagram note to singer Diljit Dosanjh saying he was hurt by the singer's June comments on the protests and asking to end the row, News18 and Hindustan Times report. Our grade: reported. Hindustan Times and News18 have it, but we can't yet count them as independent confirmation.

Albania. On October twenty-eighth, Albania's government has presented its 2027 tax package, dropping an earlier plan to raise corporate income tax, cutting VAT on 54 basic foods from 20% to 6% while raising the standard rate to 21%. We grade that reported: so far only Tirana Times has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation.

Canada. Imperial Oil's chief executive said he is encouraged by progress toward a binding Pathways carbon-storage agreement with Ottawa and Alberta, a condition for the Pacific Link pipeline, though "there's still a lot of work left to do," BNN Bloomberg reports. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, BNN Bloomberg, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.

Italy. Tens of thousands marched in Rome, Milan and other Italian cities on Friday against the cost of living and military spending, NBC News reports, as the USB union and others called public- and private-sector strikes. We grade that reported: so far only NBC News has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation.

France. On October twenty-fourth, the interior ministry says 410,000 people protested nationwide on Saturday, including 110,000 in Paris, in marches over the cost of living and the high-school movement; the CGT union puts both figures at nearly double the official count. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, Al Jazeera, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.

The Cockroach Janta Party movement. At the opening Delhi show of his India tour, singer Diljit Dosanjh answered critics of his June remark distancing himself from the CJP's NEET protests, saying “Don't teach Punjabis how to fight”, and raised the censorship dispute over Satluj, his film about activist Jaswant Singh Khalra, Deccan Chronicle reports. We grade that reported: one source so far, not yet independently confirmed.

Albania's student protests. On October twenty-eighth, Tirana’s Chamber of Commerce and Industry and Pro Export Albania oppose the government’s proposed 2027 fiscal package, which the Albanian Daily News says would raise dividend tax from 8% to 15% and tourism VAT from 6% to 10%; it also cites a corporate income tax rise to 17%, which Tirana Times reports was dropped before the package was formally presented on October twenty-eighth. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, Albanian Daily News, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.

Canada's Pacific Link pipeline fight. On October twenty-sixth, Carney, most premiers and Assembly of First Nations leaders held their first such meeting since 2005; Carney said ministers will work with First Nations on moving beyond the Indian Act. We grade that reported: CP24 and Turtle Island News carry it, but we haven't yet established that their reporting is independent.

Italy's student and cost-of-living protests. On October twenty-eighth, a Milan judge orders the release of the alleged administrator of the Movimento 17 Ottobre Telegram group, held since October twenty-fourth on suspicion of incitement, saying there are no serious grounds to believe he committed the offences; Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni calls the decision "shameful", Reuters reports. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, Reuters, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.
That's the briefing. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com.
